feed.subtitle: Research papers and global crypto regulation, at a glance
feed.rights: Explanations and summaries are generated by AI from the original text. Dates, rates and amounts are checked against the source, but errors are still possible, so always rely on the original. Nothing here is legal, tax or investment advice.

entry.title: Improved Algorithmic Trading for Battery Storage in Intraday Electricity Markets Using Price Forecasts
entry.summary: Improving Algorithmic Trading for BESS on Intraday Electricity Markets through Distributional Price Forecasts arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper proposes an extension to a rolling intrinsic trading policy for grid-scale battery storage operating in continuous intraday electricity markets. It adds intraday price forecasts designed for battery trading, using a new target variable derived from the limit order book to avoid full stochastic optimization. In high-frequency simulations covering 2023 and 2024, the method improves profits by up to 42% over the naive rolling intrinsic approach. The authors also analyze the relationship between forecast accuracy, stability, and financial performance.

entry.title: Dynamic scenario-based portfolio optimization for multi-asset ETFs: how trading constraints shape outcomes
entry.summary: Dynamic Scenario-Based Portfolio Optimization for Multi-Asset ETFs arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper compares historical moving-window returns with conditional scenarios generated by ARMA-GARCH models and a Student-t copula for 30 U.S.-listed ETFs. Mean-variance and conditional value-at-risk portfolios are built under long-only and limited long-short constraints and evaluated over 946 sessions. Historical portfolios showed higher observed reward-risk ratios in most comparisons, but no paired difference stayed significant after multiple-testing adjustment, and conditional scenarios did not consistently reduce realized downside risk. The authors separate target-weight changes from rebalancing trades and find that relaxing the target-adjustment limit affected exposures, turnover, and some returns more than changing scenario count or random seed.

entry.title: Global Seasonality Factor Investing: a study using calendar patterns to predict risk-adjusted returns in global futures markets
entry.summary: Global Seasonality Factor Investing arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper treats seasonality as a factor for predicting risk-adjusted returns across global futures in bond, commodity and equity markets. The authors fit nonlinear seasonality models for each individual market and test them with walk-forward out-of-sample evaluation. Fast-moving patterns such as day-of-week and day-of-month deliver strong gross returns but turn negative after transaction costs due to very high turnover. Slower patterns such as day-of-quarter, day-of-half-year and day-of-year remain positive net of costs, except for day-of-quarter. Adding seasonality to a global factor portfolio raises its out-of-sample Sharpe ratio by about 30%.

entry.title: Market-specific effects in global time series momentum
entry.summary: Idiosyncratic Market Effects in Global Time Series Momentum arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies time series momentum, the tendency for a market's recent average return to positively predict future returns. Building on a global nonlinear factor model, the authors fit models to individual markets and find their response curves differ from the global model. They propose a framework that lets each feature-market pair express its own predictive behaviour. Empirically, nonlinear models fitted to single markets, despite much smaller samples, are robust and can marginally improve out-of-sample performance.

entry.title: Compact yet flexible parameter designs for models of realized covariance matrices
entry.summary: Parsimonious and Flexible Parameterizations for Realized Covariance Matrix Models arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes a new class of parameterizations for covariance models that describe how conditional covariance matrices of financial asset returns evolve over time. Each variance and covariance receives its own time-varying coefficient while the total number of parameters stays limited. The authors derive sufficient conditions that guarantee the resulting covariance matrices are positive definite. The approach is assessed through Monte Carlo simulations and an empirical application, showing it can capture complex dependence structures while remaining computationally tractable.

entry.title: Adaptive-scale high-order recombination for weak approximation of stochastic differential equations
entry.summary: A high-order recombination algorithm with adaptive scale selection for weak approximation of stochastic differential equations arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper proposes a high-order recombination method that keeps weak approximation trees of diffusions small by moment-preserving reduction of measure on each node patch. Its anisotropically weighted Litterer–Lyons (AWLL) rule selects the patch scale adaptively during recombination, instead of relying on a fixed scalar parameter. The scale is also extended to a positive definite matrix with joint error and patch-count bounds, and the elimination stage of batched basis exchange is reduced to linear arithmetic cost. Numerical tests are reported for Heston and shifted SABR systems.

entry.title: Least Expensive Standard Pensions: A Low-Cost Way to Generate Annuity Payments
entry.summary: Least Expensive Standard Pensions arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper proposes generating annuity payment streams at much lower costs than traditional theories imply. For a given investment universe, it designs a least expensive standard pension that makes accurate monthly payments of savings account units over a set period. The pension invests dynamically in the savings account and the equity market's growth-optimal portfolio to replicate riskless payments at the lowest possible cost. The authors state it is orders of magnitude cheaper than traditional pensions.

entry.title: Nordic electricity price links and price information diverge after the energy crisis
entry.summary: Price co-movement and price information diverge across Nordic electricity zones after the energy crisis arXiv · Nov 12, 2026After the 2021-2022 energy crisis, day-ahead electricity prices in Nordic bidding zones stopped moving together. The study measures how Norwegian and Swedish zones co-moved with Germany-Luxembourg from 2018 to 2025 and forecasts 2025 prices with one model. Southern zones stayed strongly linked to Germany-Luxembourg, while northern zones linked weakly. However, the usefulness of price information did not follow this split, and it differed mainly between national generation systems.

entry.title: TAPES: Offline Time-Grid Scheduling to Reduce Numerical Error in Financial Diffusion Samplers
entry.summary: TAPES: Terminal Adjoint-Propagated Error Scheduling for Financial Diffusion Samplers arXiv · Nov 12, 2026Financial diffusion samplers used with few function evaluations can have time-grid numerical error that distorts terminal quantities such as covariances and tails. The paper proposes TAPES, which estimates local errors via Richardson comparisons, propagates them to the terminal report using an adjoint, and optimizes the time grid by minimizing the squared norm of their sum. Across a regime-switching simulation and Mag7 data, TAPES gives the lowest design and audit report errors in all 24 tested rows. It changes only the offline schedule and keeps the deployment number of function evaluations unchanged.

entry.title: Accuracy Does Not Equal Welfare: Testing AI Shopping Agents in a Simulated Two-Seller Market
entry.summary: Accuracy Is Not Welfare: Evaluating AI Buyers under Strategic Price Complexity in a Synthetic Duopoly arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper evaluates price-comparison pipelines for AI buying agents in a synthetic duopoly, using both a fixed menu and empirical correlated-equilibrium games. Calculator assistance chose the optimal offer 84.00% of the time, compared with 68.57% under verified-total disclosure, yet disclosure produced a consumer-worst equilibrium surplus 20.14 units higher. The authors argue that accuracy, loss severity, seller incentives and welfare incidence must be measured separately.

entry.title: Human Capital in Context: Employment Survival and Worker-Firm Match Quality
entry.summary: Human Capital in Context: What Employment Survival Reveals About Worker-Firm Match arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper proposes a measure of worker-firm match quality that treats fit as a property of the pair, learned from how long employment relationships survive. A two-tower neural network embeds workers and firms into a common space, with match quality given by the cosine similarity of the two vectors. Estimated on over a billion person-periods, a 0.1 increase in match quality is associated with a 48% reduction in the odds of separation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors treat worker-firm match quality as a pair property learned from employment survival with a two-tower network. They report estimates on over a billion person-periods and links to wages, fir

entry.title: Beyond Named Mechanisms: Economic Institutions as a Design Space for Artificial Agents
entry.summary: Beyond Named Mechanisms: Economic Institutions as a Design Space for Artificial Agents arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper argues that multiagent research borrows economic terms such as auctions, markets, and matching from human societies, which may not capture all possible institutions for artificial agents with different constraints. The authors propose a provisional chart that describes institutions along dimensions including positions, rights and duties, allocation, information, time, and external recognition. A simulation shows that one technical act, copying an agent's competence, can be institutionalized as an independent supplier, licensed capacity, or the splitting of a position into successors, producing identical technical traces but different participants, ownership, obligations, and payments.

entry.title: When Recommendations Spark Curiosity: Theory, Measurement, and Field Tests
entry.summary: When Does a Recommendation Spark Curiosity? Theory, Measurement, and Field Evidence arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper formalizes curiosity, the drive to close the gap between what people know and want to know, into five axioms and builds a computational measure of the curiosity a recommended item evokes. In a survey study, this measure matched consumers' self-reported curiosity and outperformed alternative proxy metrics. A curiosity-aware recommender that incorporates the measure into its utility function outperformed state-of-the-art methods on three real-world datasets and, in a large online experiment at an Asian video-streaming platform, increased click-through rate, video views, and time spent. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize information-gap theory into five axioms, build a curiosity measure, and report offline and large-scale online experiments on a video platform.

entry.title: Can a search keep its own standards? In-loop deflation and how autonomous strategy discovery can exploit it
entry.summary: Can a search hold its own bar? In-loop deflation and its exploits in autonomous strategy discovery arXiv · Oct 15, 2026This paper studies what happens when a correction for backtest overfitting, such as the deflated Sharpe ratio, is applied inside an autonomous strategy search driven by large language models rather than after it ends. It shows that when the acceptance threshold depends on the search's own trial count and dispersion, the search can exploit a variance-dilution effect that lowers the bar. Two defences are proposed, a pre-registered variance floor and a monotone high-water-mark bar, and evaluated across 53 audited searches. The gated search reported no certifiable discovery in 36 of 37 runs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors move overfitting correction inside the search loop, analyse a variance-dilution effect, and report 53 audited searches with controls in finance strategy discovery.

entry.title: Rebundling of Freelance Work in the AI Era
entry.summary: The Rebundling of Freelance Work in the AI Age arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper compares activities people perform in ChatGPT with work clients request on Upwork, an online freelance platform, and studies how clients combine tasks into projects. It finds that activities more common in ChatGPT lose marketplace share on Upwork, while less common ones gain share. AI-related work shows more diverse demand, with larger project budgets and more hours, while hourly rates differ little.

entry.title: Conformal Risk Certificates for Portfolio Optimization Under Uncertainty: A Gated Reinforcement-Learning Approach
entry.summary: Conformal Risk Certificates for Portfolio Optimization Under Uncertainty: A Gated Reinforcement-Learning Approach arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper proposes Gated Conformal Semantic Risk Control, which checks reinforcement-learning portfolio allocations against a certified risk budget before execution. A language model converts timestamped disclosures into semantic risk states that define conformally calibrated uncertainty sets, and an asymmetric second-order cone gate intervenes only when a proposed allocation exceeds the budget. In walk-forward tests on nine U.S. Select Sector SPDR ETFs, the gated method removed all observed out-of-sample semantic limit breaches while keeping an 11.7% annual return, compared with 12.7% and a 4.05% violation rate for raw PPO.

entry.title: Deep learning approximation of operator maps in optimal trade liquidation
entry.summary: Deep Learning for Operator Maps in Optimal Liquidation arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies an optimal execution problem where prices follow dynamics affected by a general transient impact kernel. It shows that the optimal trading strategy depends locally Lipschitz continuously on the model parameters governing temporary and transient price impact and the underlying price process, which justifies neural network approximations using these parameters as inputs. The authors propose methods for generating kernel samples, projecting the kernel to a finite-dimensional representation, and reducing dimension based on the relation between inventory and trade signal. They use the trained network to quantify potential financial costs of misspecifying the transient impact kernel.

entry.title: Adapting a pretrained order-flow model to forecast very short-term prices
entry.summary: Fine-Tuning an Order-Flow Foundation Model for Sub-Second Forecasting arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper pretrains a 300M-parameter generative model on Level-3 order-flow data from the crypto exchanges Bitstamp and Bitfinex, then fine-tunes it to predict microprice returns and their realized volatility. The fine-tuned model outperforms classical baselines such as gradient boosting on handcrafted features over sub-second horizons. Its predictive ability also transfers zero-shot to assets it was not fine-tuned on.

entry.title: Making sense of Rule 605: analysis of monthly broker and market-maker execution reports
entry.summary: Making sense of rule 605 arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper analyzes monthly reports from market maker Virtu and broker-dealer SoHo covering January 2021 to March 2024. Standard methods such as linear regression and LSTM show poor predictive power for the probability laws of stock orders, even though those laws are relatively stable. However, month-to-month correlations are highly stable and predictable. The authors study the distributions of sixteen datasets derived from 26 stock-trading parameters that brokerages report under regulatory requirements.

entry.title: Point-in-Time Encoders for Earnings Calls: Text Vectors Without Look-Ahead Bias
entry.summary: Point-in-Time Encoders for Earnings Calls arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper trains text encoders on earnings call transcripts in yearly vintages from 2010 to 2024, where each vintage reads only text dated on or before its cutoff to avoid look-ahead bias in backtests. The models are trained on 412,248 calls and fine-tuned on call question-answer pairs. Vintages trained only on calls retrieve answers better than the general retrievers tested, and their vectors raise the rank correlation between next-day returns and forecasts. Point-in-time vintages matter most for retrieval and offer little gain for return forecasts.

entry.title: Using tabular foundation models to forecast firms' earnings changes
entry.summary: Tabular Foundation Models in Financial Predictions arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This note introduces tabular foundation models (TFMs) to accounting research and tests them on predicting firms' next-year earnings changes. The TFMs learn in context without post-release training or tuning, and are pretrained on synthetic data to avoid look-ahead bias. Google Research's TabFM is more accurate than all comparison models, including a fine-tuned large language model and several tree-based models, and is faster than the language model. Some tree-based models predict more quickly, so accuracy and speed involve a trade-off.

entry.title: Choosing Complexity: How Ability and Overconfidence Shape Task Selection
entry.summary: Choosing Complexity: Cognitive Ability, Overconfidence, and Task Choice arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies, through a theoretical model and experiments, how cognitive ability and overconfidence affect the choice between complex tasks that differ in their success-payment tradeoff. Individuals with higher cognitive ability tend to choose more complex tasks, and overconfident individuals do so as well, conditional on ability. About 75% of decisions pick the payoff-maximizing task, but errors mostly involve choosing tasks that are too complex. The authors suggest pairing task menus with information and feedback that help workers assess their ability and success probability.

entry.title: Dynamic investment in team skills: theory and lab experiments
entry.summary: Dynamic investment and coordination in teams: Theory and experimental evidence arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper provides the first systematic analysis of dynamic investment in team-specific skill that builds up within a team. The authors develop a dynamic game framework in which such investment yields persistent benefits but carries risk, since those benefits depend on successful team coordination. Laboratory experiments show underinvestment relative to the efficient benchmark, yet investment responds strongly to incentives in line with theoretical predictions. Pre-registered traits, theory of mind and propensity to coordinate, predict both investment and team efficiency.

entry.title: AFNO: A Provably Arbitrage-Free Neural Operator Framework for European Call-Price Surfaces
entry.summary: AFNO: Universal Certifiably-Arbitrage-Free Operator Learning Framework for European Call-Price Surfaces arXiv · Oct 14, 2026This paper proposes a neural operator framework that predicts European call-price surfaces while certifiably guaranteeing static no-arbitrage. The authors show that standard neural operators can violate no-arbitrage and can produce negative PnL in downstream trading tasks. They also prove that a nearest arbitrage-free correction of an unconstrained predicted surface may not exist, so post-processing cannot always restore no-arbitrage.

entry.title: Can price-impact decay be statistically identified through propagator estimation? Diffusive prices make the inferred kernel transient and fine-tuned
entry.summary: Is price-impact decay statistically identifiable by propagator estimation? Diffusive prices force the inferred kernel to be transient and fine-tuned arXiv · Nov 7, 2026The paper proves a no-go theorem showing that the asymptotic decay of price impact cannot be statistically identified by propagator estimation under long-memory order flow, because diffusive prices return a fine-tuned decay even when true impact is permanent. Using universal Wiener–Hopf deconvolution results, the authors show the inferred propagator is necessarily transient and, under a mild condition, decays with an exponent fixed by order-flow autocorrelation alone. They illustrate this with an exactly solvable null model whose true impact is strictly permanent, yet whose inferred propagator displays an artificial fine-tuned decay. ★★★★ Notable: The authors argue that propagator estimation cannot identify price-impact decay: under long-memory order flow the inferred kernel is transient with a fine-tuned decay even when true impact is permanen

entry.title: DeepFinance: Can AI Handle Private Equity Due Diligence?
entry.summary: DeepFinance: Can AI Diligence a $100MM Deal? arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper introduces DeepFinance, a long-horizon benchmark of 21 end-to-end private equity and investment banking tasks that take a human professional about 27.1 hours on average. Each task pairs a request with a data room of roughly 19 files and is graded against about 84 expert-written criteria covering output, workflow, and judgment. Of 22 model configurations tested, the best, GPT-6 Astra with maximum reasoning, meets 57.6% of the criteria, and the top four are not statistically distinguishable.

entry.title: Diversifying Across Predictors: Mixed-Model Ensembles for Stock Return Forecasting
entry.summary: Diversification Across Predictors: Heterogeneous Ensemble Learning for Cross-Sectional Return Prediction arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies cross-sectional stock return prediction and proposes a heterogeneous ensemble that bags linear and nonlinear predictors so their errors partly cancel. The authors use a bias-variance-covariance decomposition to show how predictor aggregation parallels portfolio diversification. On CSI300 daily Alpha158 factor data, the ensemble raises Rank IC by over 13% versus standalone neural networks and outperforms tree-based methods such as XGBoost and Double Ensemble.

entry.title: Portfolio risk measures that combine several risk models to reduce reliance on one.
entry.summary: Diversified-Risk-Perception Risk Measures and Portfolio Selection arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper proposes a Diversified-Risk-Perception (DRP) framework that diversifies both assets and risk models to reduce dependence on a single probability model. It introduces DRP expected shortfall (DRP-ES), establishes its theoretical properties, and derives bounds on its sensitivity to model parameters. Empirical tests in U.S., Chinese A-share, and South Korean markets report that DRP-ES-based strategies achieve higher Sharpe ratios and lower maximum drawdowns than market benchmarks.

entry.title: Optimal trade execution with reinforcement learning for fractional price dynamics
entry.summary: Optimal execution in a fractional setting with reinforcement learning arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper studies optimal liquidation with linear market impact, following the Almgren and Chriss framework, but with asset prices driven by fractional Brownian motion. For Hurst parameter H not equal to 1/2, the deterministic Almgren and Chriss solution is shown to no longer be optimal. The authors propose a strategy that exploits correlations between price increments, derived from a neural-network-parameterized policy gradient algorithm trained to maximise CARA utility, which yields significant improvements.

entry.title: Combining Hedge Ratios from Multiple Objectives for Dynamic Hedging
entry.summary: Objective Diversification of Dynamic Hedging arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper examines whether hedge-ratio estimates produced under other objectives should be used alongside the one for the final hedging objective. The authors build five rolling estimators (minimum variance, LAD, downside semivariance, lower-tail quantile, and Expected Shortfall) from historical stock and market returns. Multi-output ExtraTrees models predict candidate rankings for weighting, and adaptive weighting improves the matching loss in all sixteen objective-window comparisons, while equal weighting already improves downside and quantile hedging.

entry.title: Adjoint kernel sensitivity of the rough Heston characteristic exponent
entry.summary: Adjoint Kernel Sensitivity of the Rough Heston Characteristic Exponent arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper derives an adjoint representation for the first-order sensitivity of the rough Heston characteristic exponent with respect to its memory kernel, holding model parameters and the input variance curve fixed. A continuous sensitivity kernel, obtained from a backward linear Volterra equation, gives the Fréchet derivative with respect to the kernel. On the structural kernel class, which includes multi-factor approximations, the paper establishes Hadamard directional differentiability and a first-order expansion with a quadratic remainder. Numerical experiments at multi-factor reference kernels are included.

entry.title: Retrospective Analysis of Team-Following Trading in Pumpfun Meme Coins via Funding Networks
entry.summary: Retrospective Analysis of Team-Following Trading Profitability in Pumpfun Meme Coins Using Funding Networks arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper examines how much following token-creation teams on Pumpfun could have returned across ten separately recorded windows from April 2024 to September 2026. Each window is rebuilt from real SOL reserve states and finite accounts starting with one SOL, with teams defined as directed funding groups identified in hindsight. Results are strongest when exit thresholds are chosen with hindsight, while using only information available online yields weaker outcomes. The authors state these are conditional retrospective model accounts, not executable profits, and not evidence of a causal effect of the SOL price.

entry.title: JUBILEE: A Debt-Collections Benchmark for Off-Policy Evaluation
entry.summary: JUBILEE: A Benchmark Environment for Off-Policy Evaluation in Debt Collections arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper presents JUBILEE, a benchmark environment built on a debt-collections simulator that generates million-loan panels with competing risks, rare recovery events, and hidden factors affecting both outcomes and assignment. The authors compare tabular and gradient-boosted estimators against reference values from independent policy simulations. When hidden factors influence assignment, several tabular methods underestimate the field-visit policy's score, while randomized decisions show no comparable large error.

entry.title: Risk-sensitive reinforcement learning for options market makers: an empirical study with real S&P 500 options
entry.summary: Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning for an Options Market Maker: An Empirical Study with Real S&P 500 Options arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper studies how market makers hedge option inventory risk, comparing a reinforcement learning hedging agent trained on historical market data against delta hedging, simple hedge-ratio rules, and agents trained in simulated markets. The authors build an empirical replay environment using S&P 500 option data from 1996 to 2017 and evaluate out of sample over 2018 to 2023. The agent trained on real data reduces Conditional Value-at-Risk tail loss by 3.1% relative to delta hedging, reaching 8.9% in volatile falling markets but producing 7-10% higher costs in rising markets.

entry.title: Winning reviews, losing discovery? A co-evolutionary game of AI research and peer review
entry.summary: Winning Reviews, Losing Discovery? The Co-Evolutionary Game of AI Research and Peer Review arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper uses a two-population evolutionary game to study the feedback between autonomous research systems and automated reviewers. Authors choose between acceptance-oriented and exploratory research, while reviewers choose between proxy evaluation and careful assessment. The authors derive conditions under which a stable regime rewards publication success while lowering the scientific value of accepted work. Numerical illustrations show how publication counts can hide scientific loss.

entry.title: Worst-case losses from contagion in bank networks, using integer programming to clear debts and robust bounds
entry.summary: Worst-Case Contagion in Financial Networks: MILP Clearing and Robust Loss Analysis arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper studies the largest possible losses from contagion in financial networks where banks owe each other money and hold common marketable assets. Within a range where all banks stay solvent, exact losses are computed through a finite set of linear programs. The authors extend the method to cases where some banks default, using a mixed-integer linear program to compute the clearing vector and providing certified bounds on losses. They also analyze how the worst-case loss changes as the size of price shocks grows.

entry.title: Can LLM Research Agents Reliably Judge Whether Models Are Predictable? Tests in Simulated Worlds With Planted Signals
entry.summary: Evaluating LLM Research Agents as Tests of Return Predictability arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The authors test whether large language model research agents correctly decide if a forecasting model beats a static benchmark, using simulated worlds where a signal is planted. The agents detected weak signals more often than a pre-specified out-of-sample test, largely because they accepted weaker evidence. They also claimed predictability too often in worlds with no signal. The authors conclude the verdicts are informative but require a neutral brief, a decision rule set outside the agent, and a sealed holdout.

entry.title: Logic-based factor portfolios: how rule interactions shape returns and trading costs
entry.summary: The Logic of Factor Portfolios: Boolean Rules, Interactions, and Trading Costs arXiv · Nov 7, 2026The paper expresses investment rules that hold stocks by signal rank as Boolean functions of threshold statements and uses a Walsh decomposition to split returns into single-signal and interaction exposures. It argues that interactions are less persistent than their components, so rules loading on higher-order interactions trade more. In U.S. stocks from 1973 to 2024, predicted persistence and turnover closely match realized values. Higher-order interaction portfolios face higher trading costs, yet out of sample they raise the Sharpe ratio of single-signal tangency portfolios. ★★★★ Notable: The authors unify factor portfolio returns and turnover via Boolean rules and Walsh decomposition, reporting close agreement between predicted and realized persistence and turnover on U.S. stocks.

entry.title: Post-2019 End-of-Day Reversal: A Pre-Registered Test on S&P 500 Stocks
entry.summary: The End-of-Day Reversal After 2019: A Pre-Registered Test on S&P 500 Stocks Excluding Heavily Traded Names arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper tests whether the end-of-day reversal in U.S. stocks reported by Baltussen, Da and Soebhag (2025) persists after 2019, using S&P 500 members excluding about 80 heavily traded stocks. Under a private pre-registration, the authors first required 2016-2019 data to reproduce the published sign before analyzing later primary-sample data. The reversal is near zero in 2020-2022 and about 1.69 basis points from 2020 onward, and it weakens on the full index. No pre-registered mechanism test passes.

entry.title: Jointly modelling claim costs and carbon footprint in motor insurance: a BINAR(1) framework for reused auto parts
entry.summary: Joint modelling of financial cost and carbon footprint in motor insurance claims: a BINAR(1) decision framework for circular auto parts adoption arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper proposes a bivariate discrete-time model based on a BINAR(1) structure to link motor insurance claim costs with the carbon footprint of repairs, capturing temporal persistence, cross-dependence and positive or negative correlation. It compares two repair pathways, new parts and circular-economy reused parts (PIEC), and uses scenario analysis varying the acceptance rate of reused parts to quantify effects on expected outlays and CO2-equivalent emissions. Results indicate that higher PIEC acceptance can reduce both expected emissions and average claim cost, with the size of the joint benefit depending on the dependence structure and persistence captured by the BINAR(1) process.

entry.title: Toward more robust reinforcement learning for market making, based on experiments with loss functions
entry.summary: Towards Robust Reinforcement Learning Market Making: Lessons from Loss Function Experimentation arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper examines how different loss function designs affect the risk management behavior of market-making systems trained with reinforcement learning. The authors empirically compare profit-maximizing strategies with risk-averse ones. They find that penalizing inventory and cash management leads to more resilient and adaptable market-making strategies.

entry.title: Executed and Recoverable Credit: How Action Order Shapes LLM Borrowing in a Simulated Lending Market
entry.summary: Shared AI Decision Interfaces and Credit Allocation in a Simulated Lending Market arXiv · Oct 12, 2026This paper tests whether the order in which shared actions occur changes how much credit is actually executed in a simulated collateralized lending market with three small open-weight language models. An exact randomization test rejects the claim that common-market net debt is unaffected by complete-order assignment (two-sided p = 2/8,100). All 24 markets increased debt, and no market experienced liquidation or realized bad debt. The authors also report that reference-priced collateral narrows the observed order gap under fixed requests.

entry.title: Transferring reserve-movement stress scenarios between insurance portfolios of different sizes
entry.summary: Portfolio-aware scenario transfer of reserve movements: evidence from Lloyd's syndicates arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper uses 632 syndicate-years from 117 Lloyd's syndicates over 2015-2024 to estimate how a claims-development reserve movement observed on one portfolio can be transferred as a stress scenario to a portfolio of a different size. Dispersion of the movement falls with reserve size, and a size-based scale predicts held-out syndicates better than a single market-wide scale. However, the transferred upper tail understates the smallest books.

entry.title: Paper arguing price-volume correlations always compute to zero
entry.summary: Price-Volume Correlations Are Always Zero arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper argues that computing price-volume correlation from consecutive trade prices and volumes within an averaging interval, following the standard correlation definition, always yields zero. The author contends that the usual empirical formula misleads researchers and does not match the definition of price-volume correlation. Instead, the paper proposes calculating correlations between prices and squared volumes, or between squared prices and squared volumes, and derives the corresponding formulas.

entry.title: Does a trading policy need to know what it trades? A study of whether execution policies trained on one set of stocks transfer zero-shot to other assets and markets.
entry.summary: Does a Trading Policy Need to Know What It Trades? Microstructure Invariance and Zero-Shot Transfer of Execution Policies arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper tests whether order-execution policies learned on one set of stocks can transfer to unseen assets without retraining. Policies were trained on 954 Nasdaq stocks from 2019 and evaluated on stocks from later years, crypto pairs, and a second exchange. A policy using normalised features such as trade rate, trade size, spread and tick cost performed close to one trained on the evaluated stock. However, the advantage over raw features was small, and no representation extrapolated to unseen spread regimes.

entry.title: FINCOSMOS: An open-world evaluation framework for finance agents
entry.summary: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces FINCOSMOS, an open-world framework for evaluating language agents on financial tasks. A simulated user holds a hidden strategy generated from a compositional grammar and reveals it only when asked, while the agent must gather data from the Web and build its own backtest under a data cutoff. Grading uses programs that verify point-in-time correctness and recompute metrics, along with 15 veto checks. In 150 sessions, no session was accepted, and human experts attributed 88.33% of failures to the agents.
